title: Luca Kernel-Native Network Observatory: coverage, overhead, correlation, anomaly evidence, failure handling
statement: These questions, procedures, metrics and pass thresholds were written before any experiment was run. run_experiments.py reads the thresholds from this file and records its SHA-256 in every result. Any later change must be appended to amendments with its date and reason; results produced under an earlier version keep that version's digest.

scope.environment: Three Linux network namespaces joined by veth pairs on one host (tests/netns.py): a device, an access point running the collector and the capture, and a remote network. In CI this host is a virtual machine.
scope.applies_to: The kernel, libbpf build and virtual topology recorded in each result.
scope.does_not_apply_to: Wi-Fi hardware, hostapd, real device populations or production traffic. veth devices have no radio, different offloads and no driver queues of a wireless card.
scope.synthetic_fixtures: Unit-test fixtures are never used as experimental results.

tools.capture: tshark if installed, otherwise tcpdump; filter "tcp or udp" as in Luca's capture.py
tools.zeek: zeek -C -r capture.pcap when installed; criteria that need it are reported not_evaluable otherwise
tools.editcap: used only by C4 to delete a known number of packets from a copy of a capture

A.title: Detection coverage
A.question: Which ground-truth traffic classes does each telemetry path record: the TC classifiers, the kfree_skb drop program and the TShark capture with Luca's filter?
A.procedure: One session: collector (attach auto, 0.5 s sampling) and capture on ap0; the device runs tests/traffic.py client, which generates 3 TCP connections, 20 UDP echoes, a UDP datagram with TTL 63, a UDP datagram from an unassigned source (dropped by rp_filter), 3 ESP packets, 3 ICMP echoes, 3 UDP datagrams and 1 TCP SYN to closed ports of the access point, and 3 IPv6 UDP datagrams to a closed port.

criteria.statement: The kernel classifiers record all 7 packet classes (tcp, udp, ttl63, foreign_source, esp, icmp, ipv6) with their generated packet counts.
The capture records the TCP/UDP classes (tcp, udp, ttl63, foreign_source, ipv6) and none of esp and icmp.

When the drop program attaches, the closed-port UDP drops (>= 3) and the rp_filter drop (>= 1) are keyed; on kernels >= 5.17 they are named NO_SOCKET and IP_RPFILTER. Not evaluable when the drop program does not attach.
Per-direction socket-buffer counts on ap0 equal the device veth's tx/rx packet counters within 3 packets.

descriptive: number of ground-truth classes visible only in kernel telemetry

B.title: Overhead
B.question: What does the collector cost the forwarding path and the host?
B.procedure: 5 repetitions of each condition, interleaved (baseline, collector, baseline, ...). Each repetition: a 5 s TCP bulk download from the remote network to the device (throughput at the receiver), then 2000 sequential UDP request/response round trips (latency at the device). Collector condition: attach auto, default limits, 1 s sampling, BPF run-time statistics off. A separate session with --prog-stats measures the per-invocation cost of the programs.

criteria.statement: Median TCP throughput with the collector is at least 90 % of the baseline median.
The median of per-repetition median UDP round-trip times rises by at most 25 microseconds.
No collector repetition loses telemetry: flows_not_recorded, drops_not_keyed, parse_errors and snapshot_failures are 0 and the timeline is not truncated.
Collector CPU time is at most 2 % of the session's wall-clock time in every repetition.
Collector maximum resident set size is at most 65536 kB in every repetition.
BPF map memory is at most 64 MiB at default limits.

descriptive: mean BPF run time per invocation of each program (BPF_ENABLE_STATS)
throughput and latency of every repetition

C.title: Correlation
C.question: How do kernel observations correlate with the capture and Zeek, and does the correlator stay conservative where it cannot be sure?
C.procedure: C1-C2 use experiment A's session with Zeek. C3 uses a NAT session: the access point masquerades traffic leaving through up0, the collector observes up0 (allowlisted uplink) and the capture observes ap0; the device runs tests/traffic.py client. C4 uses a paced UDP echo session (200 round trips, 10 ms apart) and deletes 20 consecutive packets lying between two kernel samples from a copy of its capture with editcap.

criteria.statement: Every TCP/UDP flow the device initiated in session A is CORRELATED and corroborated; no correlation is ambiguous and no flow is capture-only.
Every kernel-only observation states a reason, and the ESP and ICMP observations name the capture filter.
Across the NAT boundary no Zeek connection is matched to a kernel flow with a different remote endpoint, and no match is labelled corroborated.
The unedited capture of the paced session is assessed consistent.
After deleting k = 20 packets between two kernel samples, the assessment is incomplete and the proven loss is between 1 and k.

descriptive: corroborated, uncertain, ambiguous, kernel-only and capture-only counts per session
unique remote-only match rate across NAT

D.title: Anomaly evidence on labeled scenarios
D.question: Do the KNO heuristics fire on real kernel data exactly where the scenario's label says, with the provenance the design assigns?
D.procedure: Six sessions, one per tests/traffic.py scenario, each starting with the same benign TCP/UDP baseline: benign (adds ICMP to the access point itself), icmp (ICMP echo to a remote host), tunnel (ESP), forwarded (UDP with TTL 63), spoof (UDP from an unassigned source), twostacks (TCP with initial TTL 128). Expected findings: none, KNO-01, KNO-02, KNO-03, KNO-04, KNO-05.

criteria.statement: Every labeled finding is produced in its scenario (recall 1.0 over the 5 positive labels).
No finding is produced outside a scenario's label set (0 false positives over the 6 scenarios).
KNO-03 and KNO-05 are INFERRED; KNO-01, KNO-02 and KNO-04 are OBSERVED.

limitations: Designed scenarios show that the rules fire as specified on kernel data. They do not estimate false-positive or false-negative rates on real devices.

E.title: Failure and recovery
E.question: When kernel instrumentation fails, does Luca's capture keep working, and is the loss reported instead of hidden?
E.procedure: Separate sessions, each with a concurrent root capture where noted: E1 collector run as user nobody without capabilities, during a 100-round-trip UDP echo (captured); E2 collector run as user nobody with only CAP_BPF, CAP_NET_ADMIN and CAP_PERFMON; E3 collector given a BTF path that does not exist; E4 --max-flows 32 --max-drops 8 with 200 distinct UDP flows and 50 distinct closed ports; E5 ap0 deleted during collection; E6 collector killed with SIGKILL during a captured echo, in tc mode (then --detach-only) and in the default mode (then a new collector started); E7 luca-observatoryd run as user nobody with the three capabilities, driven by luca_observatory.client. E1, E2 and E7 run as transient systemd services (systemd-run with User=, AmbientCapabilities=, CapabilityBoundingSet= and NetworkNamespacePath=), the mechanism the installed unit uses; they are not evaluable without systemd.

criteria.statement: Without capabilities the collector exits 2 with a failed snapshot that states the error; the capture holds all 200 echo packets; the correlated summary reports the telemetry as UNAVAILABLE and contains no CORRELATED flow.
With only CAP_BPF, CAP_NET_ADMIN and CAP_PERFMON as user nobody the collector attaches, counts the traffic and stops cleanly.
With no usable BTF the classifiers still count traffic, the drop program is reported unavailable and the summary lists drop reasons as unsupported.

Under table pressure flows_not_recorded > 0 and drops_not_keyed > 0 are reported, the flow table holds exactly its capacity, aggregate counters still match the veth within 3 packets, and the summary reports the unattributed packets.
When ap0 disappears the collector exits 4 within 3 s with status interface_lost and keeps the counts collected before.
After SIGKILL the capture still holds all echo packets; in tc mode the filters that survive are removed by --detach-only; a new collector attaches and counts traffic.

The service, unprivileged except for the three capabilities, starts and stops a session for the client, which copies the snapshot and records status stopped; with the service stopped the client records unavailable instead of failing.
